title: Predecessor input materializer
description: Objective: select exact accepted predecessor results and produce immutable NodeInputManifest trees with revocable witness rechecks. Deliverable: runner materialization modules and fault tests. NOT in scope: provider execution or fan-in integration. Hard dependencies: Dependency contract kernel, Clean workspace foundation, and Evidence receipt pipeline. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/materialization/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner test.
definitionOfDone: Every selected result, artifact, witness, environment, and graph epoch is digest bound.
Revoked or changed inputs require a new materialization/attempt and stale trees cannot dispatch.
Duplicate or ambiguous producer selection fails closed.
taskRails: Graph Beta cannot activate until the proven Foundation runner contracts it consumes are green.
A dependency, readiness, fairness, or semantic claim without daemon-verifiable evidence is UNKNOWN or refused.
Keep tasks file-disjoint where possible; order is a presentation hint, not a fabricated hard dependency.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400; explicit paths only and no sibling worktree.

implementationPlan.description: RED — dependency witness mirror tests, before the module exists. THE CENTRAL DESIGN CONSTRAINT: @moe/runner depends only on @moe/contracts, and packages/scheduler/src/dependencies/dependency-contract.ts is neither reachable (not exported from the @moe/scheduler root) nor addable (a dependency edit would need package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml, outside this task's owned paths). So the witness surface is MIRRORED structurally, exactly as packages/runner/src/supervisor/lease-mirror.ts mirrors fenceAuthority. Read that file's doc comment first: the mirror must be a RE-VALIDATION, never a shape cast, because comparing fields on an unparsed object accepts records the authority's own parser refuses. Tests to write: a hostile-shape battery (null prototype violation, extra key, missing key, wrong type, getter-bearing object) each refused with its specific code at layer WITNESS; stability parsed as exactly "MONOTONIC" | "REVOCABLE" and nothing else; consumptionHorizon parsed against the mirrored DEPENDENCY_GATES list with "MATERIALIZATION_SEAL" present; and THE FAIL-CLOSED NORMALIZATION — dependency-contract.ts:248 downgrades a MONOTONIC contract to REVOCABLE when no monotonic-registry proof is supplied, so assert the mirror does the same. A mirror that skipped it would exempt from recheck a witness the authority treats as revocable, which is a divergence in the unsafe direction.
implementationPlan.note:
RED confirmed and for the right reason: "Cannot find module './dependency-witness-mirror.js'" — 1 failed suite, 855 passed elsewhere, exit 1. No production module exists yet.

30 tests written across 4 describes. Hostile battery is 17 table-driven cases, each asserting BOTH that the parser returns null AND that the recheck surface converts that to RUNNER_MATERIALIZATION_CONTRACT_MALFORMED at layer WITNESS — so the code is pinned on the production surface, not only on the parser. Cases: custom prototype, extra key, missing key, wrong type, getter-bearing property (returns REVOCABLE on the first read and MONOTONIC on the second — the exact smuggle a shape cast would admit), array in place of record, nested witness extra key, duplicate witnessRef, negative witness version, short witness digest, empty witness list, un-nameable node key, unknown source operation, unknown consumption horizon, "MONOTONIC " with trailing space, lowercase "revocable", oversized witness list.

Parity is asserted in BOTH directions. A null-prototype record with valid own data properties must be ACCEPTED, because the scheduler's own isPlainRecord (runtime-shape.ts:16) accepts prototype===null; a mirror that refused it would diverge just as badly, only quietly. Verified against the authority's source before writing the assertion.

The MONOTONIC downgrade (dependency-contract.ts:248) is pinned three ways so no single implementation shortcut can satisfy it vacuously: effectiveStability returns REVOCABLE with an empty registry; it returns REVOCABLE when the registry entry matches on predicateRef but NOT on schemaVersion; and behaviourally the downgraded contract is actually RECHECKED — a bumped witness version refuses WITNESS_VERSION_CHANGED — while a proven MONOTONIC contract is exempt and stays satisfied under the same bumped version. Also pinned dependency-contract.ts:245: a proven MONOTONIC contract whose witness sourceOperationClass disagrees with the registered predicate must refuse MONOTONIC_OPERATION_MISMATCH, or the mirror would be strictly more permissive than the authority.

MIRRORED_DEPENDENCY_GATES is compared against a hand-written 11-element array, not one derived from the module under test, with MATERIALIZATION_SEAL asserted at index 0. Determinism is pinned by shuffling: the first failing witness is named identically under both input orders, and the rechecked list comes back sorted under both contract orders.

Two ceilings are separated deliberately — an oversized contract list refuses CONTRACT_LIMIT while every element is individually valid, so only the bound can be answering; an oversized witness list inside a contract refuses CONTRACT_MALFORMED, which is parity with the authority's own denseArray/MAX_ITEMS behaviour.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN — dependency-witness-mirror.ts. Parse-then-validate: every parser returns null on a hostile shape and the caller picks the code and layer, the effect-parse.ts convention. Expose the MATERIALIZATION_SEAL recheck used by the seal step: given the mirrored contracts and the caller-supplied current witness facts, return either a satisfied verdict or a refusal naming the first witness that failed and why. Preserve the MONOTONIC-without-proof downgrade. Do NOT import @moe/scheduler under any circumstance — if a needed shape seems unmirrorable, report_blocked rather than adding a package dependency. Keep under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. typecheck exit 0, test exit 0, 27 files / 891 tests — up from the 26 / 855 baseline, so +1 file / +36 tests. All 30 step-3 tests pass; zero regressions.

PER-FILE CAP FORCED A SPLIT, and this is the one deviation from the plan's module list. The single module reached 407 lines, past epic rail 5's hard 400 split line, so it is now two files, each well under the 250 target: dependency-witness-mirror.ts (232 lines) owns the mirrored SHAPE — pinned literals, the five interfaces, and the four parsers, every one returning null per the effect-parse convention with no refusal vocabulary of its own; witness-recheck.ts (200 lines) owns the VERDICT — resolveStability, effectiveStability, parseContracts, compareWitness, and recheckMaterializationSealWitnesses. Rail 5 says per-file violations are fixed by splitting the file, so this is the prescribed remedy, not scope growth. Step 9 now owes five bridges, not four.

readBoundedList went into materialization-kernel.ts rather than into either mirror file: it is generic shape reading with no domain meaning, it pairs directly with the ceiling constants already declared there, and predecessor-selection needs it too — putting it in the witness mirror would have made selection import from the mirror for no reason. It reports LIMIT and MALFORMED as DIFFERENT kinds because they are different facts, which is what lets an oversized list refuse CONTRACT_LIMIT while a hostile one refuses CONTRACT_MALFORMED. The ceiling is compared against the declared length before any element is read.

No @moe/scheduler import — verified by grep; all nine matches in this directory are inside doc comments naming what is mirrored. No child_process, Date.now, Math.random, or new Date either. Reused the existing hostile-shape readers from ../supervisor/effect-shape.js (exactRecord, readOwnDataProperty, readList, isPlainArray, isCount, isRef, isDigest, oneOf) rather than duplicating them; recovery/recovery-contract.ts:1 is the precedent for that cross-directory import.

Where the mirror and the authority can differ, it differs only closed: isRef here bounds length and requires NFC text where the authority takes any non-empty string, and isCount imposes a ceiling the authority does not. So this mirror can refuse a contract the scheduler accepts, never accept one it refuses. Both normalizations from the authority are preserved — the :248 MONOTONIC-without-proof downgrade and the :245 operation-class mismatch refusal.

One fail-closed choice the plan did not specify: when a witnessRef is named by one MONOTONIC contract and another REVOCABLE one, it is reported rechecked and NOT exempt. The strictest contract naming a ref decides.

implementationPlan.description: RED — predecessor selection tests, before the module exists. This is DoD 3, the fail-closed half. Design line 380 fixes the rule: order is the graph base, then transitive accepted predecessor results in topological then stable-nodeKey order, EACH ARTIFACT IDENTITY EXACTLY ONCE. Assert: (a) a deterministic selection over a fixed closure is byte-identical across repeated calls and independent of caller input order — shuffle the input and assert the same output sequence; (b) two distinct producers offering the same artifact identity is AMBIGUOUS and refuses with its own stable code at layer SELECTION, never a silent pick; (c) the same artifact identity reachable twice through different paths is DEDUPED to one entry, which is a different outcome from (b) and must have its own test so the two are not conflated; (d) a predecessor whose result is not ACCEPTED at or above the required qualifying milestone is refused, not skipped; (e) an oversized closure refuses on the bound before any element read. Every case asserts the code AND the layer. The ordering assertion must compare against a hand-written expected sequence, never one computed by calling the function under test.
implementationPlan.note:
RED confirmed for the right reason: "Cannot find module './predecessor-selection.js'" — 1 failed suite, 891 passing elsewhere, exit 1.

38 tests across 4 describes, every failure case asserting code AND layer as an exact object so an extra or missing field fails too.

(a) DETERMINISM. Ordering is asserted against a HAND-WRITTEN sequence ["art:alpha","art:zulu-first","art:zulu-second","art:bravo"], never one computed from the subject. The fixture is built so the expectation can only hold if all three ordering rules are live: node/alpha and node/zulu share topologicalIndex 1 so the nodeKey tie-break decides between them; node/bravo has a higher index but a lexicographically earlier key, so a pure nodeKey sort would move it first and fail; node/zulu lists its artifacts in reverse so the within-producer identity sort has to reorder them. Then all four permutations of the closure assert the same sequence, and canonicalJson of two calls is compared for byte-identity via the production canonicalizer.

(b)/(c) DEDUPE VS AMBIGUITY, six tests, deliberately never sharing a case. Deduped: the same producer record reached twice yields one entry; a two-artifact producer listed twice yields two. Ambiguous with detail = the colliding identity: two distinct producers offering one identity; two distinct producers offering one identity WITH IDENTICAL BYTES (identical bytes are not identical provenance — accepting this would let the manifest bind an adoption identity chosen by list order); one identity offered with two different digests. Plus one nodeKey carrying two disagreeing producer records, detail = the nodeKey, which is a different detail from the artifact cases.

(d) MILESTONE. Below required refuses MILESTONE_UNQUALIFIED with detail = nodeKey — refused, not skipped. Exactly-at and above both accept, so the rank comparison cannot be a plain equality or an off-by-one. The unqualified producer named is the first in SELECTION order, asserted under both caller orders.

(e) BOUNDS, three separate ceilings that cannot substitute for one another: an oversized closure refuses CLOSURE_LIMIT; an over-full artifact list on one predecessor refuses ARTIFACT_LIMIT with detail = nodeKey; and a closure where every candidate and every artifact list is individually legal but the total exceeds MAX_SELECTED_INPUTS refuses SELECTION_LIMIT — only the aggregate bound can answer that one.

Also 13 table-driven hostile candidate shapes (custom prototype, extra key, missing key, wrong type, getter that returns node/alpha once then node/other, negative topological index, empty artifact list, un-nameable node key, unknown milestone, short artifact digest, negative byte length, artifact extra key, duplicate artifact identity inside one predecessor), a non-array closure, an unknown requiredMilestone, a non-commit baseIdentity, full freezing including nested entries, and an empty closure accepted as a legal base-only selection.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN — predecessor-selection.ts. Pure function over a caller-supplied closure: validate bounds, parse each candidate predecessor record, refuse on ambiguity, dedupe by artifact identity, and emit the deterministic ordered selection (graph base first, then topological, ties broken by stable nodeKey). Carry each selection's producer attempt, epoch, and adoption identity through to the output, because the seal step must digest-bind them per design line 380. Return a frozen result: either the ordered selection or one refusal. No I/O, no filesystem, no Git — this module decides WHAT is selected; the scratch-worktree materialization itself is not in this task's scope. Keep under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. typecheck exit 0, test exit 0, 28 files / 927 tests — up from 27 / 891, so +1 file / +36 tests, zero regressions.

Split again for the per-file target, same remedy as step 4: the single module landed at 281 lines, over the 250 target though under the 400 hard line, so it is now predecessor-candidate-parse.ts (144 lines, "is this a well-formed candidate record" — total parsers, one coded refusal, nothing throws past the boundary) and predecessor-selection.ts (161 lines, "which are selected and in what order"). Every production file in this directory is now under 250. Bridge count owed by step 9 is six.

Pure function throughout — no filesystem, no Git, no clock, no I/O of any kind. Ordering is applied ONCE, up front in parseClosure, so every later refusal names an element chosen by selection order rather than by the order the caller happened to build the closure in; that is what makes the two "names the first unqualified producer in selection order, not caller order" assertions hold under both permutations.

Dedupe and ambiguity are decided by one canonical producer binding per nodeKey. An identical record continues past; a disagreeing one refuses AMBIGUOUS naming the nodeKey. Because an identical producer has already continued by then, any artifact-identity collision reaching the inner loop is necessarily a genuine disagreement between DISTINCT producers, so that refusal names the artifact identity. That is a structural argument, not a comment: the two paths cannot be reached by the same input.

ONE TEST FIXTURE WAS WRONG AND I FIXED THE FIXTURE, NOT THE CODE. "refuses one artifact identity offered with two different digests" built both records under the same nodeKey, so the producer-record check answered first with detail "node/alpha" rather than "art:one". The production behaviour is right and strictly more precise — one node offering two disagreeing records is a better fact than one of its artifacts colliding. The case is now split in two, each pinning a different detail: distinct nodeKeys with different digests refuses naming the ARTIFACT, and one nodeKey with different digests refuses naming the NODE. Pinning both means a later reordering of those two checks cannot silently change which fact a caller is told.

Selection carries producer resultRef, attemptRef, epoch, and adoptionRef through to every entry, which is what the seal step must digest-bind per design line 380; the full entry shape is asserted as an exact object so a dropped provenance field fails.

implementationPlan.description: RED — manifest seal and staleness tests, before the module exists. This is DoD 1 and DoD 2. Digest binding (design line 256): assert the sealed manifest's binding hash changes when ANY of these changes, one mutation per assertion so a single over-broad digest cannot pass by accident — a selected result identity, a producer adoption identity, an artifact identity, a witness ref, a witness VERSION, a witness digest, an environment-manifest requirement, or the graph/binding epoch. Assert the converse too: re-sealing identical inputs yields an identical digest, so the digest is deterministic and not seeded by anything ambient. Staleness (DoD 2): a manifest sealed against witness version N is NOT dispatchable once the current witness is version N+1 — assert the refusal code and layer STALENESS, and assert the result carries no dispatch affordance at all by checking its key set, not by checking a boolean is false. Same for a changed predecessor digest. Assert a REVOCABLE witness is rechecked at seal and a MONOTONIC one with valid registry proof is exempt — and that the downgraded MONOTONIC-without-proof case IS rechecked.
implementationPlan.note:
RED confirmed for the right reason: "Cannot find module './input-manifest-seal.js'" — 1 failed suite, 927 passing elsewhere, exit 1.

47 tests across 5 describes.

DoD 1, DIGEST BINDING. 18 mutations, ONE FIELD PER ASSERTION, covering every item design line 256 lists: selected result identity, producer adoption identity, producer attempt identity, producer epoch, artifact identity, artifact digest, artifact byte length, graph base, witness ref, witness VERSION, witness digest, environment-manifest requirement, node authority hash, provider-runtime observation, an ABSENT provider-runtime observation (null must bind differently from a digest, so a later attempt that resolves one produces a different hash — the fail-closed direction), graph revision, graph epoch, and binding version. The three witness mutations move the CURRENT fact in lockstep with the contract, or the recheck would refuse and the digest assertion would never be reached — that is the trap that would have made three of these vacuous. On top of the per-field assertions, one test collects all 19 hashes into a Set and asserts size === 19, so a digest that changes but collides also fails; that test also asserts MUTATIONS.length > 0 so a sweep generating zero cases cannot pass silently. The converse is pinned too: re-sealing identical inputs yields identical inputTreeDigest, manifestSha256, and inputBindingHash, which no clock- or random-seeded digest could satisfy. Plus manifestSha256 must differ from both other digests, proving it does not cover itself.

DoD 2, STALENESS. The exported revalidateSealedManifest predicate is asserted for witness version N vs N+1, moved witness digest, vanished witness (all WITNESS_STALE), changed predecessor digest, changed adoption ref with UNCHANGED bytes (identical bytes are not a current adoption), vanished predecessor bytes (all PREDECESSOR_STALE with detail = artifact identity), moved graph epoch (EPOCH_STALE), a manifest field mutated after sealing so its own digest no longer covers its body, and an object that is not a manifest at all (both MANIFEST_TAMPERED). Every one asserts code AND layer STALENESS.

NO DISPATCH AFFORDANCE is asserted by KEY SET — Object.keys(result).sort() must equal exactly ["code","detail","layer","message","ok"] — not by checking a boolean is false. A refused seal cannot hand a caller anything dispatchable at all, per design line 799.

Witness recheck at seal is pinned as a WITNESS-layer refusal, not SEAL, so the layer says which gate answered. All three stability paths are covered: REVOCABLE rechecked, proven MONOTONIC exempt (seal succeeds under a bumped witness version), and downgraded MONOTONIC-without-proof RECHECKED — the :248 rule asserted through the seal surface, not only through the mirror.

Also 8 SEAL-layer input-validation cases (non-selection, bad authority hash, bad provider runtime, non-array/duplicated/oversized environment requirements, malformed graph epoch, graph epoch with an extra key). The makeSelection fixture throws rather than returning a degenerate value if selection ever refuses, so a broken fixture cannot make the whole file pass vacuously.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN — input-manifest-seal.ts. Seal the NodeInputManifest over the ordered selection: run the MATERIALIZATION_SEAL witness recheck first, then compute inputTreeDigest and the input binding hash via canonicalDigest over an explicit digest-input record, following the inputManifestDigestInput(body) shape already used in workspace-contract.ts — a named body-to-record function, so what is bound is reviewable in one place rather than implicit in a spread. Bind exactly what design line 256 lists: selected predecessor result and adoption identities, artifact identities, witness IDs/versions/digests, environment-manifest requirements, and the source graph/binding epoch. Return a frozen sealed manifest or one refusal; a refused seal produces no manifest and no dispatch affordance, per design line 799 (stale input triggers no worker claim). Expose the staleness check as a separate exported predicate so a caller can revalidate an already-sealed manifest without re-sealing. Keep under 250 lines; split the digest-input builder into a sibling module before 400.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. typecheck exit 0, test exit 0, 29 files / 972 tests — up from 28 / 927, so +1 file / +45 tests, zero regressions. Production files: input-manifest-digest.ts 243, input-manifest-seal.ts 158, manifest-staleness.ts 150. Every production file in this directory is now under 250; eight modules, eight bridges, verified present by ls.

THE ONE DESIGN DECISION WORTH REVIEWING — each bound field appears in EXACTLY ONE digest-input record and reaches the others transitively, which is the workspace-contract.ts:141 precedent ("the result body embeds both upstream digests, which is what transitively binds..."). I chose this over listing every field in every record for a concrete reason: a field bound twice cannot be mutation-tested, because removing it from one record leaves the sibling still covering it and the suite stays green. Under single coverage, deleting any field from any of the three builders reddens.

The chain: inputTreeDigestInput binds manifestVersion, baseIdentity, requiredMilestone, and the ordered entries with all eight provenance fields; nodeInputManifestDigestInput binds manifestVersion, inputTreeDigest, and the witness bindings (design line 218's set); inputBindingDigestInput binds manifestVersion, nodeAuthorityHash, the manifest digest, inputTreeDigest, environmentRequirements, the provider-runtime observation, and the source graph/binding epoch (design line 256's set). The digest module's doc comment maps line 256 ITEM BY ITEM to where each is bound, including which are transitive, so the step-11 item-by-item review is one read rather than a chase.

Tamper detection recomputes ALL THREE digests, so there is no field the manifest carries that a post-seal mutation could change without being caught — that is what closes the hole transitive binding would otherwise open.

Recheck runs BEFORE anything is bound, so a flipped witness yields a refusal rather than a manifest that faithfully records the flip. A refused seal returns only {ok, code, layer, message, detail}: no manifest key, no binding hash, nothing dispatchable, per design line 799.

DELIBERATE STRICTNESS, flagged for QA: revalidateSealedManifest refuses on ANY witness movement, monotonic or not. The MONOTONIC exemption is implemented where design line 382 puts it — the recheck AT SEAL — and line 382 is explicit that "a current or accepted attempt cannot adopt a changed witness in place". A manifest already sealed against a specific version and digest is exactly that case, so a bumped monotonic version requires a new materialization rather than in-place adoption. Documented in the function's doc comment with the reasoning, not just the behaviour.

Split twice for the per-file target, same remedy as steps 4 and 6: the seal reached 286 lines, so staleness revalidation moved to manifest-staleness.ts. That split earns its keep beyond line count — a caller holding a sealed manifest must be able to re-ask "may this still dispatch" WITHOUT re-sealing, since re-sealing would cheerfully produce a fresh manifest over the moved facts and hide the exact movement the check exists to catch.

implementationPlan.description: Runtime bridges. @moe/runner now carries 45 tracked .js bridges package-wide (task-eb9ff081), so every new non-test module here needs its sibling bridge or the package becomes unloadable by plain Node again. Add one per production module — materialization-kernel.js, dependency-witness-mirror.js, predecessor-selection.js, input-manifest-seal.js — each exactly one line, `export * from "./<name>.ts";`, LF, trailing newline. Test files get NO bridge. CRITICAL: the vitest gate is structurally blind to a missing bridge because Vite resolves ./foo.js to foo.ts while Node does not, so a green suite is not evidence here. Prove it with a plain-Node probe from the repo root and record all three controls: POSITIVE — each new bridge imports and its namespace has more than zero non-default exports, none undefined; REGRESSION — an existing bridged module still loads; NEGATIVE — a path with no bridge still raises the literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, proving the probe can still detect failure.

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW FOUND FOUR REAL FAIL-CLOSED GAPS. All fixed, all mutation-verified, none were caught by the 975 tests that were already green. git diff was empty because every file is new, so I read the sources as an attacker instead.

1. FORGED SELECTION BYPASSED THE AMBIGUITY REFUSAL — the worst one. sealNodeInputManifest took a typed PredecessorSelection and re-parsed only its shape, so a caller who never called selectPredecessorInputs could hand it a record binding ONE artifact identity to TWO producers, and it sealed. DoD 3's fail-closed refusal was avoidable by simply not using the selector. This is the lease-mirror trap applied to my own boundary: comparing fields on an unparsed object accepts what the real parser refuses. parseSelectedInputs now enforces "each artifact identity exactly once" itself. Mutant: 1 failed.

2. REGISTRY PROOFS RESOLVED BY LIST ORDER — parseMonotonicRegistry accepted two entries for one (predicateRef, schemaId, schemaVersion) and registry.find took the first. The authority refuses duplicates outright (dependency-contract.ts:189), so the mirror was MORE PERMISSIVE than what it mirrors — the one direction the mirror doc comment says is a bypass rather than a convenience. Two disagreeing proofs could have exempted a witness from recheck by ordering. Now deduped-refused. Mutant: 1 failed.

3. ONE WITNESS DECLARED TWICE AT DIFFERENT VERSIONS WAS PICKED SILENTLY — the recheck kept the last binding seen for a repeated witnessRef, so two contracts disagreeing on a witness version or digest resolved by contract order and sealed against a value the other contract never agreed to. Structurally identical to the ambiguous-producer failure this task refuses elsewhere, and inconsistent to refuse one and not the other. Now refuses CONTRACT_MALFORMED at layer WITNESS naming the witness. A converse test asserts an IDENTICAL repeated declaration still passes, so the check cannot be satisfied by refusing every repeat. Mutant: 2 failed.

4. STALENESS PARSERS USED BARE typeof — currentWitnessFacts and currentPredecessors accepted NaN, Infinity, -0, and unnormalized text where every sibling parser uses isRef/isCount. Fail-closed by luck (NaN !== anything, so it refused) rather than by construction. Tightened, and the wrong ceiling constant (MAX_MATERIALIZATION_CONTRACTS where witnesses were meant) corrected.

DIGEST OMISSION, CHECKED ITEM BY ITEM against design line 256: nodeAuthorityHash, manifest digest, input tree, environment requirements, provider-runtime observation and graph/binding epoch bound directly in inputBindingDigestInput; selected predecessor result and adoption identities via inputTreeDigest; witness IDs/versions/digests via manifestSha256. planningNotes.risks:
THE SUBTLEST TRAP — dependency-contract.ts:248 normalizes a MONOTONIC contract DOWN to REVOCABLE when no monotonic-registry proof is supplied. That is a deliberate fail-closed default. A mirror that copies the stability field verbatim and skips the downgrade will exempt from recheck a witness the authority considers revocable, and it will do so silently, in the unsafe direction, with a green suite. Step 3 pins it with its own test.

MIRROR DRIFT IS UNTESTABLE FROM HERE — a verdict-equality test against the real validateDependencyContract cannot live in @moe/runner, which cannot import @moe/scheduler. Child 1 hit the identical wall with lease-mirror and deferred its drift test to the daemon package, which depends on both. Ship hostile-fixture parity here and flag the drift test as follow-up work for a package that can see both sides; do not fake it with a local re-declaration, which would assert the mirror against itself.

DEDUPE VERSUS AMBIGUITY ARE DIFFERENT OUTCOMES — the same artifact identity reached twice by different paths is deduped to one entry; two DIFFERENT producers offering the same artifact identity is a fail-closed refusal. Folding them into one code would let a genuine conflict pass as a dedupe. They get separate tests for that reason.

DIGEST BINDING IS EASY TO PASS VACUOUSLY — assert one mutated field per assertion. A single test that changes several fields at once cannot distinguish a digest that binds all of them from one that binds only the first.

BRIDGES — the package now has 45 tracked .js bridges and no build step. New modules without them make @moe/runner unloadable by plain Node, and the vitest gate cannot see it (mem:gotcha-vitest-hides-missing-js-bridge). Step 9 probes with all three controls; a probe that only imports the new modules passes vacuously.

SHARED WORKTREE — during the mutation drill another agent's whole-tree hook can commit your drill edit, after which git status looks clean while the edit is still live (mem:mutation-drills-in-shared-worktree). Verify restoration with git diff on the specific file.
